nodes.summary: If $\rho : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is a Dickman–de Bruijn function, then $\rho$ is continuous on $[0, \infty)$.
nodes.title: Continuity of the Dickman–de Bruijn function on the nonnegative reals

nodes.summary: If $\rho : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is a Dickman–de Bruijn function, then $u \rho'(u) + \rho(u - 1) = 0$ for every real $u > 1$.
nodes.title: Delay differential equation of the Dickman–de Bruijn function

nodes.summary: If $\rho : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is a Dickman–de Bruijn function, then $\rho$ is differentiable at every real $u > 1$.
nodes.title: Differentiability of the Dickman–de Bruijn function above one

nodes.summary: If $\rho : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is a Dickman–de Bruijn function, then $\rho(u) = 1$ for every $u \in [0, 1]$.
nodes.title: The Dickman–de Bruijn function equals one on the unit interval

nodes.summary: If $\rho : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is a Dickman–de Bruijn function and $u$ is a real number with $0 \le u$ and $u \le 1$, then $\rho(u) = 1$.
nodes.title: Normalization of the Dickman–de Bruijn function, inequality form

nodes.summary: If $\rho : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is a Dickman–de Bruijn function, then $\rho(u) = 0$ for every real $u < 0$.
nodes.title: The Dickman–de Bruijn function vanishes on the negative reals

nodes.summary: There is exactly one function $\rho : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ that is a Dickman–de Bruijn function, that is, such that $\rho(u) = 0$ for $u < 0$, $0 \le \rho(u) \le 1$ for $u \ge 0$, $\rho$ is continuous on $[0, \infty)$, $\rho(u) = 1$ for $0 \le u \le 1$, and for every $u > 1$ the function $\rho$ is differentiable at $u$ with $u \rho'(u) + \rho(u - 1) = 0$.
nodes.title: Existence and uniqueness of the Dickman–de Bruijn function

nodes.summary: A function $\rho : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is a Dickman–de Bruijn function if $\rho(u) = 0$ for every real $u < 0$, $\rho$ maps $[0, \infty)$ into $[0, 1]$, $\rho$ is continuous on $[0, \infty)$, $\rho(u) = 1$ for every $u \in [0, 1]$, and for every real $u > 1$ the function $\rho$ is differentiable at $u$ with $u \rho'(u) + \rho(u - 1) = 0$.
nodes.title: Dickman–de Bruijn functions

nodes.summary: If $\rho : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is a Dickman–de Bruijn function, then $\rho(u) \le 1$ for every real $u \ge 0$.
nodes.title: Upper bound one for the Dickman–de Bruijn function on the nonnegative reals

nodes.summary: If $\rho : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is a Dickman–de Bruijn function, then $0 \le \rho(u) \le 1$ for every real $u \ge 0$.
nodes.title: Range of the Dickman–de Bruijn function on the nonnegative reals

nodes.summary: If $\rho : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is a Dickman–de Bruijn function and $u \ge 0$ is real, then $\rho(u) \in [0, 1]$.
nodes.title: Pointwise range bound for the Dickman–de Bruijn function

nodes.summary: If $\rho : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is a Dickman–de Bruijn function, then $\rho(u) \ge 0$ for every real $u \ge 0$.
nodes.title: Nonnegativity of the Dickman–de Bruijn function

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
